stories.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
stories.summary: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IBlH More men than ever are taking testosterone-boosting medication Image: BREUEL-BILD/IMAGO Advertisement Making sperm is, in large part, what testosterone is for. Which is why it is ironic when a man who doesn't need it starts taking it anyway: His brain registers an unusually high level of the hormone in his blood, concludes his body has made too much, and sends the order to stop. The testes go silent and sperm production declines. Testosterone is having a moment. It is all over social media, gym culture and wellness forums, sold by online labs, gym contacts and telehealth services.
